sectors.name: Technology
themes: Domestic liquidity is increasingly rotating into small-cap Indonesian tech names, decoupling from US tech selloffs and creating persistent alpha opportunities.
Government digitalization and data-center buildouts are durable demand drivers for local software, cloud, and infrastructure plays like ELIT and CENT.
IDX tech volatility remains high, but the +1.36% local vs -1.88% US gap signals structural preference for domestic exposure, rewarding selective bottom-fishing.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in IDX tech leaders ELIT, CENT, and AREA; their outsized gains signal domestic liquidity rotation into local names despite US weakness. Trim exposure to US-linked tech (2303) and hold JAST/KREN for momentum. Maintain normal risk posture, favor ID-listed software/telecom over hardware.

sectors.name: Financials
themes: US retail trading platforms (HOOD, IBKR) are structurally gaining share via zero-commission and crypto integration, a durable trend that lifts global fintech sentiment and Indonesian digital-brokerage
Indonesia's Sharia-compliant fintech lenders (PADI, AKSI) benefit from rising financial inclusion and Bank Indonesia's digital-payment push, creating sustained loan-growth and fee-income drivers.
Crypto exchange proxies (COIN, BMAS) are leveraged to Bitcoin adoption and US regulatory clarity, but Indonesia's own crypto-tax regime and rupiah volatility cap upside, favoring selective exposure.
sectors.ai: Buy HOOD and COIN on US retail-crypto momentum spillover into Indonesia's digital-asset proxies; PADI and AKSI offer leveraged domestic fintech beta with regulatory tailwinds. Trim BMAS on profit-taking after its run, rotate into IBKR for cross-border volume durability. Watch IDX liquidity—US strength may not translate if rupiah weakens; keep positions under 5% each.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesian coal miners benefit from sustained thermal coal price floors driven by China's import demand and domestic DMO quotas, supporting margin resilience for producers like COAL and ALKA.
Gold-linked equities such as EMAS and BRMS are structurally supported by central bank buying and rupiah depreciation, which boosts local-currency revenue conversion for Indonesian bullion miners.
Small-cap energy names like DWGL and SMMT face durable liquidity and financing constraints, making them prone to outsized moves but requiring strict position sizing and exit discipline.
sectors.ai: Buy selective coal and gold miners on strength: ALKA, EMAS, and COAL lead with volume-backed rallies, while BRMS offers laggard upside. Favor names with export flexibility and hedging upside; trim DWGL and SMMT into strength given thin liquidity. Maintain neutral aggregate exposure, rotate into high-beta producers ahead of Q3 earnings revisions.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's new RUPTL (2025-2034) mandates 75GW of new renewable capacity, creating a decade-long structural order book for domestic EPC and component makers like POWR and 373220.
Falling LCOE for solar-plus-storage in eastern Indonesia, combined with PLN's grid parity push, is unlocking off-grid industrial demand—benefiting MPOW and LAPD's captive power models.
US IRA subsidy uncertainty is redirecting global climate-tech capital toward ASEAN, with Indonesia's nickel and geothermal resources positioning local issuers as low-cost supply-chain winners.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's renewables lag is a buying window: POWR's +8.98% and 051910's +8.12% signal policy-driven momentum in geothermal and battery storage, while US weakness (-0.39%) is rotation, not rejection. Accumulate domestic names with PPAs or captive industrial off-takers; expect Q3 RUPTL revisions to catalyze 15-20% upside in compliant issuers.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rising middle-class disposable income in tier-2/3 cities continues to drive volume growth for affordable packaged foods and beverages, favoring low-priced, high-turnover FMCG names.
Digital distribution and direct-to-consumer channels are structurally lowering go-to-market costs for small-cap consumer brands, enabling faster share gains against incumbents.
Import substitution in packaging and raw materials, supported by government local-content rules, is improving gross margins for domestic producers like YUPI and BTEK.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in small-cap consumer names with confirmed volume (AGAR, YUPI, BTEK) as the sector's relative strength vs. IDX persists; rotate out of laggards into leaders with earnings catalysts. Expect mean-reversion in NAYZ/DAYA after outsized moves—trim into strength. Maintain overweight on staples for defensive positioning ahead of rupiah volatility.

sectors.name: Healthcare
themes: Indonesia's JKN (national health insurance) expansion continues to drive volume growth for domestic hospital operators like RSCH and SAME, independent of global healthcare sentiment.
Local pharmaceutical and distribution names (DKHH, MEDS) benefit from government-mandated domestic content requirements, creating durable margin protection against import competition.
US-listed healthcare (UNH, HUM) moves transmit weakly to Indonesian equities, so alpha is best sourced from idiosyncratic regulatory and demographic drivers rather than sector beta.
sectors.ai: Buy RSCH and DKHH on relative strength within a flat tape; both show institutional accumulation and Indonesia-specific demand catalysts. Trim PRIM into strength given its beta to US names. Maintain core exposure to SAME for domestic volume growth. Avoid chasing HUM; its move is sentiment-driven. Overall, stay neutral-weight, rotate into local operators with pricing power and volume visibility.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's coal and nickel export volumes are structurally rising on China's re-stocking and downstream smelter build-out, directly lifting bulk and marine logistics utilization rates.
Port infrastructure bottlenecks and draft limitations in East Kalimantan and Sulawesi create persistent pricing power for barge and tug operators with dedicated terminals.
Government push for domestic logistics digitalization and multimodal corridors favors listed players with integrated warehousing and last-mile networks over fragmented trucking peers.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian logistics names with hard-asset moats (SAFE, BLTA, TMAS) on the back of commodity export volume recovery and port-congestion-driven rate upside; trim pure-play land freight (PPGL, PJHB) after their sharp re-rates. Position for Q3 coal and nickel shipment seasonality, and monitor rupiah stability as the key swing factor for margin expansion.
